complexity.notes: The repeated maxDepth calls redo work already done by deeper calls, so each node's subtree gets re-scanned at every ancestor; a single pass returning ||both the subtree height and the best diameter found inside it|| from one recursive call would be O(n). Also, recursion depth equals tree height, so a skewed generalized tree can exceed Python's recursion limit even though the algorithm itself is correct.
complexity.summary: Top-down recursion: at each node it computes the through-root candidate as maxDepth(left) + maxDepth(right), then recurses into both subtrees, recomputing maxDepth from scratch at every node.
